title: A light-gated ozone contrast stayed below zero with a 150 ppb missing-value cap at the 80 ppb target in North Wales in 2021
abstract: We tested whether missing light records leave the sign of a heated-minus-ambient ozone exposure contrast uncertain. We used hourly records from a North Wales wildflower experiment in June to September 2021. Light was known for 1,824 of 2,928 hours; paired ozone was known for 2,926. Our index sums ozone above 40 ppb when common light exceeds 100 micromoles per square metre per second. If each missing ozone value is between 0 and 150 ppb, exact marginal bounds are -2.0865 to -0.2576 ppm h at the 80 ppb peak target and -4.6183 to +0.6108 at the 110 target. Bounds allow every unknown light gate to vary. At a 300 ppb cap, both intervals permit both signs. Three light cutoffs are reported. These are algebraic bounds under stated assumptions, not confidence intervals. One dome per treatment, shared light, source gap filling and one site-year limit inference. We test no plant response or causal climate effect. Code, aggregate results, a figure and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Marginal bounds for heated-minus-ambient light-gated excess ozone in four months and their sum. Light cutoffs are 0, 100 and 200 micromoles per square metre per second. Missing ozone values are assumed to lie in 0 to 150 ppb. Lines are possibility bounds, not confidence intervals. Complete windows give points. Panels have different horizontal scales. Contains data supplied by UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology.
